quote: Yeah. Looks like we were just giving you a call because we received a request. You're looking at solar for the home. How are you doing today?
stewart_read: The rep never states the company's full legitimacy anchor beyond 'Ion' and a vague 'we received a request' — no state framing, no certified-installer language, no reference to the specific form/channel. It works here because the customer is already compliant, but the intro's job of pre-empting 'is this a scam?' is thin.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read considered: rep may have judged the customer was already warm (missed-call callback) so a full legitimacy build wasn't needed. Supported by the customer's immediate 'Yes' with no pushback.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to keep a consistent, fuller legitimacy line even on callback leads — cheap insurance against suspicion on tougher customers.

quote: No. That's that makes sense. Yeah. I don't blame you. Is this kind of your first time, looking into solar, or have you looked into it before?
stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to the required 'what interested you in solar' question, but it's phrased as a yes/no history check rather than an open probe for motivation. The customer answers 'first time... in general' and the rep never follows up on WHY she's interested.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep may have deprioritized this because the customer is pre-move-in and hasn't experienced a bill yet, so there's less obvious pain to surface. But the schema still calls for probing motive (moving in, new homeowner excitement) as an anchor.
coaching_implication: Show the rep this is the depth-graded verify item they skipped past — even a first-time buyer has a reason (excitement about a new home, wanting to start efficient) worth capturing for the closer.

quote: Well, you know, you're about to put the aqua plant. So I'm just trying to get prepared before that aqua plant get put up.
stewart_read: The customer is a brand-new homeowner about to move in and the rep frames solar planning as getting ahead of the 'aqua plant' (likely a mishearing/transcription of a fence, patio, or similar improvement). This is a timing-alignment enthusiasm signal — a new homeowner planning property changes before moving in is a strong window for solar-inclusive planning.
coaching_implication: Rep did pick up on the timing signal in the moment, but didn't expand on it (e.g., ask what else she's planning for the property) or flag it clearly for the closer as a 'new homeowner, pre-move, planning improvements' hook.

quote: Yes. Because I was still I'm going, doing this cash doing a cash, price deal.
stewart_read: The customer raises the credit qualifier only to redirect into a cash-purchase plan — this is a moment where the rep could reinforce that a cash deal is even simpler/faster, tying it forward to the appointment. Instead the rep just acknowledges and moves to square footage.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have judged that cash-buyer status is closer-tier financial content, correctly deferring detail to the specialist. This is plausible since Ion's protocol pushes financial mechanism talk to the closer.
coaching_implication: Minor — the deferral is defensible as scope discipline, but a one-line reinforcement ('cash makes this even more straightforward, the specialist will walk you through those numbers') would have created more forward pull without violating scope.

quote: Cool. Well, we the last thing we'll need is just the square footage of the home. Do you happen to know that off the top of your head? If not, I can look it up.
stewart_read: The bill/usage question is never asked at all in this call — the rep jumps from credit qualifier straight to square footage, skipping the average-bill verify item entirely. Since the customer hasn't moved in yet, there may be no bill to reference, but the rep never even asks about her prior residence's usage or acknowledges the gap.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: because the customer hasn't moved into the home yet, she may have no ComEd bill history at that address, making the standard bill-capture step genuinely inapplicable. This is the more supported read given her 00:43 statement about not having moved in yet.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly acknowledge the bill gap for the closer ('no usage history yet since she hasn't moved in') rather than silently skipping it — this affects how the closer builds the design.

quote: K. I appreciate your time, sir. We'll look forward to speaking with you tomorrow at nine.
stewart_read: The call ends with a locked day and time (tomorrow, 9AM) and does reference the call being phone-only and needing email access, but the rep never runs the full button-up: no explicit hour-block statement, no 'is that fair?' handshake, no restated text-follow-up promise.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close every booking with the full button-up checklist (hour block, no-driving reminder already given, verbal handshake, text-confirmation promise) — the appointment is booked but the confirmation mechanics are incomplete, which the schema flags as predictive of no-show risk.
